chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Hassaan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Qassim, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

About the saying of Allah (Exalted is He): 'For when the trumpet is sounded,' he said: 'From among us there is a hidden Imam. When Allah wishes to manifest his command, He will prick him in the heart with a prick, so he will appear and rise to execute the command of Allah.'

key_terms.إِمَامًا مُسْتَتِرًا: A hidden Imam (referring to the Mahdi in occultation)
key_terms.النَّاقُور: The Trumpet (used for signaling or resurrection)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of the sounding of the Trumpet in relation to the Hidden Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) links the eschatological sounding of the Trumpet to the specific moment of the Hidden Imam's reappearance, emphasizing a divine, internal spiritual awakening ('naktah') that precedes his public emergence. This interpretation underscores the Shia belief in the Imam's occultation as a state of readiness, where his authority is activated by God's will to establish justice, distinguishing the Mahdi's appearance from general resurrection events.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (40) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash’ari from Muhammad bin Hassaan from Muhammad bin Ali from Abdullah bin al-Qassim from al-Mufadhdhal bin Umar that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had been

asked about this Qur’anic verse, “For when the trumpet is sounded,”and he had said: “From among us there will be a hidden imam. When Allah wants him to rise, He will prick him in the heart and he will appear to execute the order of Allah.”
